_comment: Lectern's filter. A posting is KEPT if any role_title word appears in its title, or if three or more topic_text words appear in its body. flex_text never causes a keep — it only annotates a kept record, because 'part-time' on its own has nothing to do with teaching. Every kept record records which words matched and where, so a reader can apply this file by hand to one posting and get the same answer. v0.2.0 (2026-09-26): added the alternative titles these roles are posted under — Developer/Designer/Creator Advocate, Design or Product Evangelist, Community Engineer, Community Architect, Product Education Manager, Technical Content Engineer, Developer Experience, DevRel, Technical Writer. Several are broad on purpose and the run report measures what noise they added. v0.2.1 (2026-09-26, same day): REMOVED 'developer experience' and 'advocacy' after measuring them. 'developer experience' fired on 11 postings and 10 were backend or platform software-engineering jobs (Anthropic, Figma, Stripe x2, GitLab, OpenAI x2, Notion, Replit, Canva) — the phrase names an engineering discipline, not an advocacy role. 'advocacy' fired once, on a customer-marketing programme. Kept: 'devrel', which found Vercel's DevRel Engineer. This is what P3 is for — the filter is a file, so a word that turns out to be noise gets cut and the cut is recorded. v0.3.0 (2026-09-26): Professor Bear refined the target — any job that DEVELOPS MATERIALS, whether to sell into universities, to teach the public, or to train the company's own people. Anthropic's 'Technical Documentation and Content Engineer, Claude Docs' is the model. Measured every candidate word against all 3,446 titles before adding: 11 of them appear in ZERO titles today and so cannot add noise; 'creator', 'documentation', and 'content engineer' each appear in exactly one title and it is the right one. 'learning experiences' found Replit's LEARNING EXPERIENCES CREATOR, a bullseye that v0.2.1 missed because it only had 'learning designer'. REJECTED as measured noise: bare 'learning' (42 titles, almost all Machine/Reinforcement Learning) and 'content strategy' (3 titles, all regional SEO marketing). v0.6.0 (2026-10-26): TWO GATES that apply after the keywords. Professor Bear, looking at a 'K12 Education Account Manager, South Korea (12 months contract), Seoul' from a design-software company: 'keep it to English-speaking countries? Unless it's France or Italy. Or Brazil? Or Portugal? And no K-12.' A posting the keywords would keep is now rejected, with its reason, if (1) location_rule: its place names no allowed country (the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Ireland, France, Italy, Brazil, Portugal), or (2) k12_rule: its TITLE says K-12. Both are data at the end of this file and collect.py only reads them. The gates never touch a posting the keywords reject, so every old reject keeps its old reason. The numbers behind each choice are in measured_before_adding; the choices that are Professor Bear's to change are named in the _comment of each rule. v0.6.1 (2026-10-28): a second judge, for a second Discord channel. Professor Bear, 2026-10-28, with a list of Unity, Unreal and Godot job titles: 'any game jobs that an early-career person who knows Unreal or Godot or Unity, or has any experience there, could take' go to a new channel, #games-3d-simulations, and posting waits until he says go. The list is the `games` section of config/targets.json (status `active` = on the list; 10 studios), not a second file; `studio_hint` below says what an early-career title at a listed studio needs to count. materials_rule._comment: Professor Bear, 2026-09-26: 'everything's probably named differently, but that kind of job would be something to look out for.' Titles cannot carry this family — 'documentation' is in 2 of 3,446 titles and 'technical writer' in zero — so a posting is also KEPT when its BODY says the job is to produce teaching materials FOR a named audience. Both halves are required: a make-materials phrase AND an audience. 'Maintain documentation' in a tax director's ad matches the first and not the second, which is the whole point. TIGHTENED same day after measurement: the first version kept 101 extra postings at roughly one-in-ten precision, because phrases like 'technical documentation' and 'technical content' appear in almost every engineering, support, and legal ad — every product has docs. Nine phrase groups were removed and the threshold raised to TWO verb-object phrases. The removed list is kept here because a rule that failed is evidence about the corpus, not an embarrassment. Final pass: threshold back to ONE phrase (two matched nothing in the whole corpus), and three more phrases cut. The surviving list is 23 phrases that only a teaching-materials job uses. Measured precision of the body rule after all cuts is in the run report; it is the only rule here whose precision was measured rather than assumed, because it was the only one that failed loudly enough to force it.

Measured on the 2026-10-18 corpus (3,243 postings) before adding: 495 titles carry an account or partnership word; 7 of those also name a university or higher education in the body; 5 of the 7 were already kept (Canva and OpenAI higher-education account roles, Anthropic's AI for Science partnership role) and 2 are new. location_rule._comment: Which countries a posting may be in. Professor Bear, 2026-10-26: English-speaking countries, plus France, Italy, Brazil and Portugal. TO CHANGE THE LIST edit allowed_countries: use a name that is a key of `countries` below. Every country the reader can recognise is already there, so adding India or Singapore is one word, nothing else. THE CHOICES THAT ARE HIS, each with the default taken and what it costs (counts: the postings the keywords alone would keep in an 84,282-posting snapshot of 2026-10-24, titles and places only: 1,056, of which this rule drops 146; on the six watched boards 58 and 8). (a) Which countries are 'English-speaking': the default is the narrow list, the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Ireland. NOT included, with what each would bring back: India 20 postings (1 on the six boards), Singapore 22 (0), Philippines 3, Hong Kong 3, South Africa 0. (b) A location that names no country ('Remote', 'Hybrid', 'N/A', 'EMEA', 'Remote - Europe') is KEPT (if_no_country_named: keep) and the record says location.country_named is false, because a place the reader cannot read should reach a person, not vanish: 50 postings in the snapshot, 2 of 82 in the 2026-10-18 run. Set it to "reject" to drop them. (c) A posting in several places is allowed if ANY one is ('Berlin, Germany | Austin, TX' is kept; a line of only foreign places is rejected; a foreign place beside one that cannot be read is kept). (d) Puerto Rico counts as the United States; 'Georgia' alone counts as the American state. HOW A PLACE IS READ, so it can be done by hand: the line is split on the separators into places; in each place the first of these that is found decides it: a country's own name or abbreviation (names), then a state or province code after a comma, hyphen or bracket ('Athens, GA' is Georgia, USA; codes), then a city or region (places). Names that are also American towns (Lebanon, Jamaica, Holland, Berlin) sit among the places, so a state code beats them. Longer names win ('New Mexico' is not Mexico). A string two countries share goes to the allowed one: a stray posting costs less than a lost one. Words in workplace_words ('Remote', 'Hybrid') are not places. Accents are ignored ('Sao Paulo'). MEASURED: against the country codes the boards themselves report, on 37,470 postings where both the board and the reader name a country, they agree on 37,458; the 12 that differ are postings in several places (the board reports one code) and the country Georgia. KNOWN WEAK SPOTS: a foreign city with no country written and not in `places` is read as 'no country named' and kept; a list is not the world, and the audit (audit/audit_gates.py) shows the unread places so they can be added.

k12_rule._comment: No K-12 roles, in any country. Professor Bear, 2026-10-26: 'And no K-12. No.' DEFAULT (narrow): the TITLE says K-12 in any spelling (K12, K-12, K–12, K -12) or names a grade band (K-8, pre-K, kindergarten, elementary, middle, high, primary or secondary school). Measured on the titles of the 84,282-posting snapshot: 212 hits, 201 at one charter-school network (not on the watch list), 6 Instructure sales titles ending '- K12', Esri 1, Canva 2 (the K12 Education Account Manager in Seoul and its twin in Vietnam), Khan Academy 1 ('Elementary School 3 - 5'), Stripe 1 ('High School Internship'). On the six watched boards: 2. TRAPS CHECKED: 'K8' is Kubernetes (3 titles, Coupang and OneTrust), so the list says 'k-8' with a hyphen and does not match it; 'K12' is also a company's name, but the company field is not read, so a company called K12 is not a K-12 role by its name. THE BODY IS NOT READ (body_phrases is empty), which is a choice that is his: 5 of the 3,243 saved ads say K-12, 4 of them are kept, and all 4 are broad education roles that also name higher education (three OpenAI Education roles: 'higher education institutions, K-12 districts, and country-level partnerships'; a Canva Indonesia education marketing role: 'across K-12 and Higher Education'). Put "k-12" in body_phrases to drop them too. NOT CAUGHT BY THE TITLE RULE: Canva's 'District Education Advocate, South Korea' in the 2026-10-18 ad was the same job before it was retitled 'K12 Education Account Manager'; its ad says 'school system' and never 'K-12'. Only the country rule dropped it.

engine_rule._comment: Which postings go to #games-3d-simulations: (a) a game, engine or real-time phrase in the TITLE (groups), or (b) a craft role at a studio on the list (studio_hint; the list is the `games` section of config/targets.json, status `active`), AND an early-career word in the title (early_career), the allowed countries and no K-12 (the two gates above apply here too). By hand: lower-case the title, blank the false_friends, look for a phrase of a group that is switched on; if a veto_word is in the title it is not early career (so 'Associate Director' is a director); if an early_career word is in the title it is early career; failing a phrase, an early-career title at a listed studio counts if it has a craft_word and none of the non_craft_words; with neither level word the level is 'not stated'. Every decision carries its reason (collect/engine_jobs.py judge_engine). MEASURED on the ai-jobs snapshot of 2026-10-24 (84,282 postings, 715 boards, titles and places only): 178 titles reach a decision. 105 name a level that is not early career (senior 58, lead 16, principal 15, staff 6, sr 4, manager 2, ii 2, sénior 1, director 1); 25 are dropped by the country gate (China 12, Spain 5, India 2, Uruguay 2, Finland, South Korea, Serbia, Japan 1 each; none by K-12); 25 name no level and are HELD BACK; 23 would be posted, 14 by a title phrase (11 Epic Games internships; an Associate Game Designer at Hasbro, Naughty Dog and Nintendo) and 9 by the studio list (Epic 3, Roblox 2, Naughty Dog 2, Riot 1, Nintendo 1). Lectern's own saved boards (3,243 postings, 2026-10-18) contain none: no watch-list company is a game studio. THE STUDIO LIST, company by company, with a keep or drop line and the reason, is section H of TARGETS.md. Kept (10): Epic Games, Riot Games, Roblox, Scopely, Supercell, Nintendo, Naughty Dog, Jam City, Kabam, Bungie. Dropped (7): Take-Two (a corporate board), Bethesda (the feed's board is a physical-therapy employer, not the game company), Twitch and Discord (not game developers; Twitch alone would add 5 engineering postings), Hasbro (toys; the phrases already find its game roles), Framestore and Foundry (film VFX). The noise it was checked for: Nintendo has 17 early-career titles and 15 are IT, retail, supply-chain, localization or manufacturing interns, all removed by the non_craft_words; an 'Associate Product Designer' at Roblox got through the first version and is now removed. WHY SO FEW: of the 51 game, film and engine companies on the feed's list that I checked, 17 have a board the feed can read, and studios post mostly senior jobs. Of the five the feed cannot read, only Ubisoft has a public board that answers (SmartRecruiters 'Ubisoft2', 324 postings; judged with these rules it would add 6 French internships); Activision is on Workday, Blizzard on Phenom, Electronic Arts on a paged HTML site, Unity's system is not identified. THE EARLY-CAREER READING is the title and nothing else (the ad text is not in the feed): it agrees with the feed's own seniority label on 162 of 163 titles the first version matched (the one difference is a 'Manager', and this rule is right), but the two rules are of one family, so that is consistency, not proof; I read every title that would be posted and all are plausible entry points. A title that states no level may be junior-friendly ('Game Programmer (1 Year Contract)') or may want five years; the title cannot say. 'Early Stage' (25 titles, startups) is blanked so it does not read as 'stage', the French word for an internship. THE CHOICES THAT ARE HIS, with the default taken: (1) posting is OFF (`posting`: "off"); a dry run shows what would go, and nothing is sent until he says go and this is set to "on" and the poster is run with --send. (2) include_unstated_level is false: the 25 with no level word are held back, not posted; true would add them. (3) The `simulation` group is OFF: it would add 10 postings (1 early career, 9 no level word); read by title, only the defense 'modeling and simulation' ones (Anduril, Shield AI) might be engine work; switch it on with "enabled": true. (4) The studio list is on, with the verdicts above; he can flip any studio by changing its verdict in targets.json (status `active` = keep, `dropped` = drop) and running ops/build_from_targets.py. (5) Ubisoft: adding it to the feed's company list is a change in the ai-jobs repository, which is his to approve. SOURCE: see the 2026-10-28 entries in HISTORY.md; the feed's rights status is a decision of his too.

consulting_rule._comment: Which postings go to #consulting-firm: a consulting ROLE word in the TITLE (role_words), an explicit EARLY sign in the title (early_career.words), no level word that is not early career (veto_words, which include Partner and Managing), no clearance in the title (clearance_words), none of the not_consulting_words, the allowed countries and no K-12 (the two gates above apply here too). A role word with no early sign ('Analyst', 'Associate', 'Consultant') is HELD BACK, not posted. By hand: lower-case the title; if no role word is there it does not match; if a not_consulting word is there it is not consulting; if a veto word is there it is senior or mid (so 'Associate Director' and 'Senior Associate' are not early career); then clearance, then country; then an early sign posts it and no early sign holds it back. Every decision carries its reason (collect/consulting_jobs.py judge_consulting). WHY A JUDGE OF ITS OWN: the main keep rule looks for teaching and training words. On the 907 postings with ad text from the four Greenhouse boards it kept 9 and none was an early-career consulting job. MEASURED on the five readable boards read once on 2026-10-28 (946 postings: Accenture Federal Services 720, Baringa 110, Brattle 58, Analysys Mason 39, Altman Solon 19; titles and places only): 38 postings would be posted, 16 distinct roles at 2 firms (Brattle Group 35 postings in 13 roles, one per city; Analysys Mason 3). 82 name a role and no early sign and are HELD BACK (Accenture Federal Services 63, Brattle 8, Altman Solon 6, Baringa 4, Analysys Mason 1). 107 name a level that is not early career (senior 79, manager 17, sr 3, architect 2, principal 2, director 1, ii 1, lead 1). 18 are not consulting roles. 36 are removed: 30 by the country gate (Germany 10, Bulgaria 10, Netherlands 2, Poland 2, Mexico 2, Norway, Sweden, Singapore, Spain 1 each) and 6 by the clearance veto. THE CLEARANCE VETO removed 6 titles, all at Accenture Federal Services ('Cleared Business Analyst', 'Secret cleared' analysts, an SAP consultant needing an active Secret clearance). Judged without it, none would have been posted and all 6 would have been held back: today it changes the held-back list, not the posts. A clearance needs US citizenship; this is about that, not about any sponsorship flag, and no sponsorship claim is made anywhere (the posts say it is not checked). THE COUNTRY GATE treats consulting offices like every other posting: 6 early-sign titles were dropped (four Analysys Mason internships and graduate roles in Germany, an Associate Consultant in Norway, a Brattle research analyst in Madrid), and Altman Solon's early-career analyst roles in Amsterdam, Warsaw and Munich fall to it too. France, Italy, Brazil and Portugal pass. Whether consulting should get a longer country list is Professor Bear's call. CROSS-CHECK: on the research session's own sample (the same boards plus the first page of 12 Workday tenants, 1,179 titles) this judge posts 44 postings, 22 roles at 5 firms; the research session's rule gave 47, 25 roles at 8 firms. The gap is two titles removed as not consulting (an office-management internship, a cyber analyst) and the exact reconciliation of the rest was not done. The Workday firms (Baker Tilly, Ankura, BRG, Booz Allen, Cambridge Associates, Guidehouse, Huron) show up only in that sample, not in what Lectern can read today. THE EARLY READING is the title only. 'Associate' is a post-MBA role at some firms and an entry role at others, so a bare one is held back; 'Associate Consultant' counts as early. A start year 2026 to 2029 in the title marks a graduate cohort (43 titles in the sample, none noise). 'co-op', 'placement', 'vacation', 'clerkship', 'entry level', 'trainee', 'campus' occur in no title today, so they cannot add noise yet. THE CHOICES THAT ARE HIS, with the default taken: (1) posting is OFF (`posting`: "off"). (2) Accenture Federal Services: the board is read and its clearance titles are vetoed; it contributes no post today and 63 of the 82 held-back titles. (3) A bare Analyst, Associate or Consultant is held back (include_unstated_level is false); true would post the 82. (4) A Workday reader is not built (10 consulting firms and 2 tagged companies, one reader). (5) Visa sponsorship is not checked and is never claimed; checking it means the Department of Labor and USCIS records, which needs downloads and his word. (6) The rest of the directory (Canyon to Z) is not pasted. (7) 'Senior Associate' and 'Senior Consultant' are not early career. (8) The 17 non-consulting companies in the list are tagged and dropped. SOURCE: collect/consulting_collect.py reads the boards of the firms in targets.json (section `consulting`, status `active`) with Lectern's own readers, one request each; the ai-jobs snapshot holds only one of those firms. See the 2026-10-28 entries in HISTORY.md.

speakers_rule._comment: Which companies go to the speakers channel (posting OFF): a COMPANY, not a posting, judged from SOURCED SIGNALS and never from words in a title (collect/speakers_judge.py). A lead needs (1) mcp_docs: the company's own public page for its own MCP, with an https link, and (2) a public contact route the company itself publishes; then the score is the sum of weights: mcp_docs 30, devrel_team 15 (a DevRel team or program page, or a job post for the role), mcp_talk 20 for the first talk about the MCP plus 5 for each further one up to +10, named_people 10 (at least one person found whose page shows them talking about the MCP; the names are in the local speaker-records/, never here), community_channel 5, and contact_route 10 if it is a DevRel page, a speaker form or a partnerships form but only 5 if it is a community forum or a public handle (a route, not one for speakers). Total 100. A score at or above min_score (60) posts; below it the company is held back, and so is one with no route. A 'to-do' company (a question for Professor Bear is open) is held back, not scored. If the links were re-checked (speakers_collect.py --check), a signal counts only if its link answered 2xx, or turned the script away (robots, 401, 403, 429) for a page the researcher OPENED; a 404 or 410 never counts. The score says how likely a company is to send someone; it is a screening heuristic and was not validated against any invitation sent, because none was. By hand: no mcp_docs link that answers means not-mcp; no route means held back; else add the weights. MEASURED on the 67 companies researched on 2026-10-30 from the companies' own pages (six research passes, then one request per link: 195 links, 179 answered 200, 10 turned the script away by robots.txt, 5 were 404, 1 was 403): 31 would be posted, 35 are held back (6 of them have talks and a named person and no published route: Docker, Notion, PayPal, Postman, Snowflake, Stripe), 1 is not-mcp (Salesforce: its docs page refused the researcher and the script, so its MCP rests on no opened page yet). At other minimums the same list posts 47 (40), 40 (50), 23 (70), 9 (80). Of the 16 links that did not answer 2xx, 5 are the researchers' own bad links (two MongoDB videos, a Datadog job post, a Zapier webinar, a GitLab evangelists page), which now count for nothing. What it cannot do: a forum is not a speaker bureau (only 3 companies have a DevRel page, speaker form or partnerships form that answers: Autodesk, Apify, Exa; GitLab's find-a-speaker page returns 404); 'opened' is the researcher's word, not the script's; a status of GA, beta or experimental is only what the page says; and no person was contacted, so willingness to speak is unknown for every company. Weights, min_score and the route kinds are settings here, not constants in the code.
